results.trace: grep DESKTOP_MIN|DESKTOP_QUERY: only src/ui/layout.ts:9,17,21. They are unused outside the module, but they are correct, documented and derived from tokens.
results.reason: Exporting two well-named, documented constants that are not imported elsewhere is harmless and a style preference. Nothing behaves wrongly, and the spec asked for the threshold to be computed in one place, which is what layout.ts does.

results.trace: src/ui/components.css .ui-keycap declares `border: var(--outline-default) solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: var(--radius-rect); box-shadow: var(--shadow-hud); background: var(--color-cream); color: var(--color-ink);`. .ui-panel (components.css:72-76) declares the same border, border-radius and box-shadow, and .ui-panel--cream (88-91) the same background and color, declaration for declaration. hud.ts already composes panel classes ('ui-panel ui-panel--mustard ui-hud-best'). .ui-keycap--primary is declared later in the file with equal specificity, so it would still override the cream background. Composing 'ui-panel ui-panel--cream ui-keycap' in keycap-legend.ts key() gives the same computed style.
results.reason: The five declarations duplicate the existing .ui-panel and .ui-panel--cream classes exactly, and composing those classes is the established pattern. The fix is safe because the primary modifier comes later in the cascade and still wins.

results.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R4-1.test.ts`. The test builds the harness screens, renders stage hud--first-lap at 1440x900 without touch, and reads getComputedStyle(.ui-keycap).borderTopWidth for all 5 keycaps. It failed with `expected Set{'3px'} to deeply equal Set{'4px'}`. The cause is that .ui-keycap uses var(--outline-default)=3px, and only .ui-keys__panel gets --desktop-outline.
results.reason: UI_RULES §3 says outlines are 4px on desktop, and §5 and the spec ask for 4px outlines on desktop. Keycaps render only in desktop mode and are 36px tall, so neither the 2px nor the 3px tier applies. They measure 3px.

results.trace: tests/ui/desktop-hud.test.ts snapshot() (lines 35-61) records posSize, lapSize, labelSizes, outlines, pos box, pause box, touchVisible and legendVisible. It never reads .ui-hud-map. The only assertion on pause is `DESKTOP.width - d.pause.right === 32` (line 95), and that holds whatever PAUSE's width, because .ui-hud__tr is right-anchored at --desktop-margin (hud.css:139-142). Deleting hud.css:170-173 (map ×--desktop-scale) or 177-180 (pause ×--desktop-scale) therefore leaves AC1, AC2 and AC6 passing. No other test file covers these rules. The spec summary requires 'the minimap and PAUSE button at ×1.45'.
results.reason: The spec's summary feature (minimap and PAUSE at ×1.45) is implemented in hud.css:170-180, but no test measures it, so a regression would go unnoticed. A new test comparing desktop and phone boxes would pass on the current code.

results.trace: src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:25-28 builds the items key-left/key-right STEER, key-up primary GAS, key-down BRAKE, and ESC PAUSE. tests/ui/keycap-legend.test.ts AC4 checks only `k.querySelector('svg')` for each of the 4 icon keys, plus the ESC text. AC3 checks labels and AC5/AC6 check visibility. icons.ts:14-17 defines distinct polygons for key-left, key-right, key-up and key-down, but no test compares them. No test checks ui-keycap--primary either. Swapping the icons or dropping the `true` primary flag leaves every test passing. The spec summary requires '↑ on rally-red, as in the mockup'.
results.reason: The right arrow-to-key mapping and the rally-red GAS key are spec requirements that no test pins down, so swapped arrows (a user-visible bug) would pass. The current code is correct, so a new test asserting them would pass.

results.trace: keycap-legend.ts:40-43 updates `desktop` through watchDesktop's 'change' listener (layout.ts:20-24). In keycap-legend.test.ts, useDevice() stubs matchMedia with an EventTarget that never dispatches 'change', and every test builds the UI after fixing the device. In desktop-hud.test.ts, AC6 opens a fresh context per viewport, and AC2 (the only resize test, lines 106-118) reads only .ui-hud-pos__n and outlines, never the legend. Replacing the watchDesktop call with a one-off matchMedia(...).matches read would therefore pass every test. The spec summary says 'the mode updates live on resize'.
results.reason: No test checks that the legend's live response to a resize works, even though the spec requires live mode updates. A browser test that resizes the first-lap stage would pass on the current code and catch the regression.
